text:
B: Hello, er, hiya. Can you hear me alright?
A: Yeah.
B: Good. I'm Callum. Taunton, in Somerset.
A: Shazia. Blackburn.
B: Blackburn. I've never been up there, to be honest. Is it nice?
A: It's alright. Bit grey.
B: Ha. Taunton's the same in winter. So, er, what do you get up to?
A: Not much. I'm not working. I was in a warehouse, packing. My back went.
B: Ah, that's no good. I've seen a few lads on site do their backs in. Lifting doors on your own, that's the killer. Has it got any better?
A: Bit. Some days.
B: Yeah. I'm a joiner, so, windows and doors on old houses, that kind of thing.
A: Mm. My husband says our windows are rotten. Landlord won't do nothing.
B: They never do. Sorry, can I ask, what's the frame behind you? The gold one. It's lovely.
A: That? It's a prayer. Ayat al-Kursi. From the Qur'an. My mum gave it me when we moved in.
B: Oh, right. It's beautiful work, the lettering. I like that sort of thing, careful hand stuff. When I was interrailing I went in all these wooden churches in Slovakia, and I couldn't read anything on the walls, but you could tell someone had spent years on it, you know?
A: Yeah. It's meant to protect the house.
B: That's nice, that. My mum's got a little cross in the hall, sort of the same idea.
A: Mm.
B: So were you born in Blackburn, or?
A: No. Pakistan. Near Mirpur. I came when I was fourteen.
B: Fourteen, that's a big move. Did you like it when you got here?
A: Erm. Not at first. School was hard. The English. It's home now, more than there.
B: Yeah. I've never lived anywhere but Somerset, so I can't imagine. Do you go back?
A: For weddings. It's a long journey. I don't like the airports.
B: No, me neither, if I'm honest. Er, what do you do with yourself, then, day to day?
A: Go to my mum's. Cook. I cook every day nearly.
B: Oh yeah? What do you make?
A: Saalan, daal, chapatis. Imran likes it hot.
B: I do a big pot of curry sometimes, but I'm sort of half following a recipe off my phone. Probably not a patch on yours. I've started making pickles, though. My stepdad's allotment had too many courgettes, so I've got jars all over my mum's kitchen.
A: Courgette pickle?
B: Yeah. It's alright, honestly. Bit vinegary.
A: You want to do achar. Mustard oil, chillies, methi. Not vinegar. My mum makes lemon one, it's...
